sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: 45Ca2+ influx assay in Xenopus oocytes: MYC-OXGR1 increased baseline Ca2+ influx and further responded to 1 mM α-ketoglutarate (αKG) vs. uninjected controls — function fully preserved (L2, PMC9294391). Surface display confirmed by confocal immunofluorescence and immunoblot (L1, PMC9294391).
sites.rationale: OXGR1 is a GPCR with no signal peptide; residues 1–34 form the extracellular N-terminus and residues 306–337 are intracellular, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus. The 'MYC-OXGR1' naming convention universally denotes an N-terminal fusion in GPCR literature, placing the tag before M1 (insert_after_residue=0). Python verification confirms residue 1 = M and TM1 begins at residue 35, giving 34 residues of extracellular buffer — well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. Two independent papers (L4, L5) with different tags (Flag; Flag+BRIL) at the same N-terminal position further corroborate this junction. MYC-OXGR1 full-length construct expressed in Xenopus oocytes (PMC9294391); no residue number stated. OXGR1 carries no signal peptide (raw topology begins 'O', residues 1–34 are extracellular); the C-terminus (306–337) is intracellular. Exactly one extracellular terminus exists, so the N-terminal prepend is the only position consistent with 'MYC-OXGR1'. Corroborated by L4 (Flag tag, HA-SP-driven N-terminal display, PMC13372822) and L5 (Flag+BRIL N-terminal fusion on full-length receptor, PMC13507345).

sources.claim: MYC‐tagged OXGR1 was detectable at or near the oocyte surface by confocal immunofluorescence microscopy (Figure 1a and b ) and by immunoblot analysis (Figure 1c ).

literature_notes: All five ledger lines converge on the same N-terminal prepend junction (insert_after_residue=0). L1 and L2 (same paper, PMC9294391) provide surface detection and functional validation respectively for the MYC-tagged construct; L3 is the construct-injection description for the same experiment. L4 (PMC13372822) and L5 (PMC13507345) independently corroborate N-terminal tagging of full-length OXGR1 with Flag and Flag+BRIL respectively. Because all lines pin the identical junction, this is one site reported once, with L1 as the primary clip. No ledger line names any residue number, so position_evidence is topology_derived throughout. The intracellular C-terminus (306–337) is not a surface-tag site and is not promoted to sites[]. No ledger line reports an insertion that abrogates function or targets an intracellular loop.
